```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(priogridR)
config <- priogrid::pg_config(nrow = 2, ncol = 3, verbose = FALSE)
```

`priogridR` keeps data conversion, quality assessment, combination, and export
in one explicit workflow. This vignette uses small offline data so that every
step can run during package checks.

## Construct two cell-period datasets

The first source has one observed missing value and several structurally absent
cell-periods. These are different conditions and should not be treated as
interchangeable.

```{r data}
climate <- data.frame(
  pgid = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021, 2021),
  temperature = c(21, NA, 22, 20)
)

population <- data.frame(
  pgid = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021, 2021),
  population = c(100, 80, 103, 82)
)
```

## Inspect metadata and structure

`pg_metadata()` reports only information that is stored in or supplied with an
object. It does not invent source provenance for an ordinary data frame.

```{r metadata}
pg_metadata(climate, config = config, time = "year")
pg_describe(climate, time = "year", config = config)
```

## Separate coverage from missingness

Coverage uses the six configured cells and two requested years as its explicit
reference. Missingness, by contrast, uses only rows that actually exist.

```{r quality}
pg_coverage(
  climate,
  time = "year",
  variables = "temperature",
  config = config,
  reference_time = 2020:2021
)

pg_missingness(climate, variables = "temperature", time = "year")
```

An absent row does not imply a measured zero. Use `pg_complete_panel()` only
when a complete panel is substantively required, and provide `fill` values
only for variables with meaningful structural zeros.

## Check compatibility and combine sources

`pg_assert_compatible()` checks grid, CRS, temporal, and key definitions.
`pg_bind()` applies these safeguards before joining variables.

```{r combine}
pg_assert_compatible(
  climate,
  population,
  config = config,
  time = "year"
)

analysis_data <- pg_bind(
  climate,
  population,
  along = "variables",
  config = config,
  time = "year"
)
analysis_data
```

Row-wise binding is also supported. Duplicate keys and conflicting values fail
by default; `conflict = "first"` or `"last"` must be requested explicitly.

## Compare versions

`pg_compare()` distinguishes keys found in only one dataset, paired missing
values, one-sided missing values, and unequal observed values.

```{r compare}
revised <- climate
revised$temperature[revised$pgid == 1 & revised$year == 2021] <- 22.25

comparison <- pg_compare(
  climate,
  revised,
  time = "year",
  variables = "temperature",
  config_x = config,
  config_y = config
)
comparison
comparison$variables
```

## Apply existing utilities and export

The checked result remains an ordinary data frame and can be passed directly
to temporal, spatial, plotting, and output functions.

```{r finish, eval=FALSE}
analysis_data <- pg_temporal_lag(
  analysis_data,
  variable = "temperature",
  time = "year"
)

pg_write_result(analysis_data, "analysis-data.parquet")
```

For a reproducible analysis, record the input data release, grid configuration,
variable semantics, transformations, and package version alongside the
result. `pg_metadata()` provides a common schema for this information, but it
cannot recover provenance that was never recorded.
